selection_rationale: Candidate retrieval from the registered seed full text and its bibliography/citation contexts only. The seed is labeled fulltext; the bibliography is seed_reference_contexts, not the cited papers' primary abstracts or full texts. The catalogue is a catalogue, not primary experimental evidence, and no catalogue identity or method merge is proposed. Nominations distinguish earlier accessibility implementations (R4/R5), biochemical and library-construction components (R10/R11), a different-transposon in vivo precedent (R12), protocol/experimental comparisons (R13/R14/R16/R23), physical protection/compaction experiments (R18/R19), and DNase footprinting precedent/comparisons (R24/R25/R26). Each reason identifies seed blocks and each evidence quote is verbatim from source seed. These are reasons to retrieve and inspect the cited works, not verified claims about their contents or admitted historical links; no direct assay ancestor is established. The existing seed extraction is reused unchanged, with only its op_tagmentation and op_purify_amplify identifiers; no before-side operation identifiers are invented. The seed's architecture combines adapter-bearing transposition, native unfixed chromatin as the assay substrate, accessibility-dependent sampling, and amplification; no single citation is assumed to establish that whole combination. Author hypotheses and explanations in [b00008], [b00012] and [b00016] are distinguished from reported comparative observations. Routine recipe uncertainty does not prevent these conceptual retrieval leads, while enzyme, substrate and interface differences remain material to any later relationship claim. General chromatin background (R1-R3/R20), regulatory-network context (R9), the ENCODE guide (R15), chromatin annotations (R17), analysis software/inference methods (R22/R27/R36-R38), IL2/drug/disease interpretation (R28-R32), and suggested RNA-seq integration (R33/R34) are not nominated solely because they are cited. Boundary cases and attribution problems are retained below.
unresolved_searches: R6 and R7: seed [b00004] introduces earlier nucleosome-positioning methods and [b00012] says the seed signal "displays characteristic phasing of upstream and downstream nucleosomes6,7". Their primary texts are not registered here. It remains unresolved whether either supplies an experimentally relevant protection/library mechanism beyond a prior phasing pattern. Keep them as possible additional nucleosome-method retrieval leads; R23 is the explicitly attributed MNase comparison dataset, not a substitute for checking R6/R7 if that narrower question is pursued.

R8: [b00004] includes it in the earlier nucleosome-positioning citation range, while [b00014] invokes it for RNA polymerase II at the nucleosome boundary. Bibliography [b00065] identifies a histone-methylation profiling study. Whether an experimental preparation in that work is relevant to the assay neighborhood is unresolved; the seed contexts alone support background/readout comparison, not a changed operation.

R21: [b00011] groups it with R2/R20 in "These data suggest that ATAC-seq reveals differentially accessible forms of chromatin, which have been long hypothesized to exist in vivo2,20,21." Bibliography [b00078] names an experimental nucleosome-surface/compaction paper. Its possible mechanistic relevance needs primary-source inspection; this grouping does not demonstrate Tn5 steric exclusion or distinguish a directly contributing experiment from chromatin background.

R35 attribution discrepancy: Figure 5 [b00100] states "ATAC-seq footprint prediction is confirmed by alignment with published NFAT ChIP-seq data (blue track, data from ref 35)." Bibliography [b00092] instead identifies Jolma et al., Multiplexed massively parallel SELEX for characterization of human transcription factor binding specificities. Do not infer the experiment from either the caption or the title alone. Resolve whether this paper actually supplies the cited NFAT ChIP-seq data. It is currently an application-validation attribution question, not an assay-architecture nomination.

Comparator provenance and quantitative claims require checking the nominated primary papers: [b00009] names DNase-seq13 and FAIRE-seq16 but co-cites 13,14 for the DNase cell-input comparison, while R14 is the FAIRE protocol. Likewise [b00016] jointly cites R25/R26 for similar footprints without assigning the exact displayed DNase dataset. R5 names a comparison locus, not necessarily a dataset source. Do not treat bibliography entries or these grouped citations as independent verification of cell inputs, preparation times, experimental provenance, or causal efficiency gains.

For R10/R11/R12, primary-source inspection is still required to resolve which enzyme variants, DNA substrates, adapter structures and amplification interfaces were demonstrated. R12 is explicitly a Hermes in vivo paper in the seed bibliography; it cannot establish purified Tn5 in vitro on unfixed nuclei. No nominated primary abstract or full text is available among the registered initial sources, so all final historical relationships remain open.

The seed Methods [b00026]-[b00031] report an Illumina transposase, custom Nextera PCR primers, qPCR-monitored amplification, a low-cell purification omission and avoidance of size selection without identifying a separate experimental predecessor reference for those choices. No additional reference or before-side operation ID is invented for op_purify_amplify. Exact recipe/interface adoption remains unresolved if later needed for a specific relationship; it does not block the explicitly cited tagmentation or comparison leads.
